hook.text: A market with one firm can still be competitive—if potential entrants can enter and exit freely.

buildup.text: In a contestable market, the threat of entry disciplines the monopolist. It prices as if competitors existed.

discovery.text: The key condition: no sunk costs. If entering and exiting costs nothing, hit-and-run entry becomes viable.

twist.text: Airlines were thought to be contestable. But airport gates, brand loyalty, and frequent-flier programs create barriers.

climax.text: Perfectly contestable markets are rare, but the theory shows that potential competition matters as much as actual.

punchline.text: The threat of entry can be enough.

quiz.question: What makes a market 'contestable'?
options: Free entry and exit with no sunk costs
